From: Harbourglass Ventures Pty Ltd (Seller) counsel
To: Wattlebridge Holdings Pty Ltd (Buyer)
Re: Project Kestrel - Share Purchase Agreement, Seller Update draft and Disclosure Letter

Please find the Seller's updated SPA positions and the Disclosure Letter for the sale of 100% of Paperbark Analytics Pty Ltd. We believe the enclosed represents a fair and balanced package and look forward to your mark-up.

SELLER UPDATE - KEY NEGOTIATED POSITIONS (Project Kestrel)

Clause 12.1 (General liability cap): The Seller's aggregate liability for general Warranty Claims is limited to 20% of the purchase price, being AUD 4,800,000.

Clause 12.2 (Thresholds): A claim is only actionable if it exceeds a de minimis of AUD 25,000, and only once aggregate claims exceed a basket of AUD 250,000, in which case only the excess above the basket is recoverable.

Clause 12.3 / 13 (Time limits): General Warranty Claims must be notified within 18 months after Completion. The Seller proposes that any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise.

Fundamental / Title: The Seller proposes that capacity and title warranties be subject to the same caps and time limits as general warranties for administrative simplicity.

Clause 9.3 / 12.8 / 20.5 (Limitations & reliance): The limitations, exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions apply to all Claims of any nature.

Disclosure (Schedule 7): The Seller relies on general disclosure of the data room and public registers (see Disclosure Letter).

Clause 8.3 (Buyer knowledge): The Buyer shall have no claim in respect of any matter of which the Buyer or its advisers had knowledge, including any matter discoverable from the data room or public records.

Clause 3 / 6.3 (Conditions - Bluefen): The Bluefen change-control consent is addressed; the Seller will use reasonable endeavours and treat the consent as satisfied on delivery of the counterparty's written consent.

Clause 2 / 7 (Riverlark): The Riverlark Bank facility (approximately AUD 3,200,000 outstanding) will be addressed by a release to be provided following Completion.

Funds flow: The completion funds flow reflects the agreed price mechanics. (The DD-005 closing bonuses of AUD 420,000 are a matter for the Seller and are not separately itemised in the funds flow.)

Clause 11.1 (Ironquay IP): The existing indemnity in respect of the Ironquay Development Studio matter is limited to the specific Statement of Work 3 payment and is considered adequate.

Clause 4.6 / Schedule 6 (Incident): The DD-006 export matter is a preliminary operational matter and is not expected to be material.

Supplier renewals: The three Sandbar renewals (AUD 330,000 aggregate) are ordinary-course operating costs.

Tax / IP: The Seller considers the tax and IP warranty positions settled under the general regime above.

Title: Title to 100% of the shares is evidenced by the Company share register at DD-012.

Project Kestrel - Seller Disclosure Letter (SPA-003). All entities, people, transactions and records are fictional.

1. General Disclosures
[1.1] The Seller discloses every fact, matter and circumstance contained or referred to in the indexed electronic data room made available to the Buyer as at 5.00pm 22 September 2026, including DD-002 to DD-012.
[1.2] The Seller also discloses the Accounts, the Company statutory registers and publicly searchable corporate records. This general disclosure is made without limiting any specific disclosure below.
[1.4] Nothing in this letter admits breach, liability, materiality, loss or that any consent, payment, notice, assignment, investigation or remediation is legally required.

2. Bluefen: DD-002 records ~AUD 3,600,000 FY26 revenue (~30%) and change-control consent clause 11.2 with conditions in 11.3. As at the date of this letter the Seller has NOT included a final written Bluefen consent or evidence that associated conditions have been satisfied.

3. Riverlark: DD-003 records ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding with change-control 8.1 and discharge 9.2. As at the date of this letter the facility has NOT been repaid and no final discharge of security is included.

4. Ironquay: DD-004 clause 7.3 conditions transfer of SOW3 Project Materials on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open; this is not independent bank verification of non-payment. No receipt of payment or confirmatory assignment is in the data room.

5. Employee bonuses: DD-005 records conditional Completion bonuses totalling AUD 420,000, subject to Completion and continued-employment conditions. Those amounts do NOT appear in the draft Completion funds flow. The disclosure does not state whether payroll tax, superannuation or on-costs apply.

6. Export/privacy incident: DD-006 records delivery of a download link to an unintended external email address; the export may contain ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps). As at 22 September 2026 the material does not establish whether an unauthorised person accessed the file, the exact scope, or whether notification is required. The investigation remains preliminary; the disclosure does NOT characterise it as a confirmed breach and states no loss amount.

7. Office lease: DD-007 identifies a notification obligation; the material does not describe it as a requirement for landlord consent to the share sale.

8. Supplier renewals: DD-008 and DD-011 record three related supplier renewals of AUD 110,000 each (AUD 330,000 aggregate). Read together for timing/scope. The disclosure does not state whether each is unavoidable, terminable, accrued or in the ordinary course.

9. Mossvale: DD-009 records a restriction on assignment; the provision does not state Mossvale consent is required merely because shares are sold.

10. Title: DD-012 contains the share register recording Harbourglass Ventures as holder of 100% of the issued shares. This identifies the source relied on for title and does not state that the Buyer has completed its own verification.

11. Reservation: No expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included. The Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts against the complete agreement and current due diligence record.
=== END SELLER DOCUMENTS ===

Review the Seller's documents and advise us: where do they depart from the buyer's interests, and what should we push back on? Identify the material issues yourself and give your reasoning. Then summarise your recommendations.

# Project Kestrel: Review of Seller's Update and Disclosure Letter

## Bottom line

The Seller's package would leave Wattlebridge with almost no recourse for the risks the Disclosure Letter itself reveals. It does this in three ways:

- General disclosure plus a constructive-knowledge bar means every known risk is carved out of the warranties.
- A blanket cap, time limit and exclusive-remedy regime covers everything, including title and fraud.
- The costly items (Riverlark debt, bonuses, Ironquay, the incident) are pushed to post-Completion or left to the Seller.

The cover note's "negotiated positions" and "fair and balanced" framing is wrong. Nothing has been agreed, so we should say so in writing and reserve our position on every point.

I have reviewed only the Seller's summary and the Disclosure Letter, not the SPA text of clauses 8.3, 9.3, 12 and 20.5. The clause-level points below are provisional until we check them against the full draft and DD-002 to DD-012.

The cover note also contradicts the Disclosure Letter. It describes Bluefen and Riverlark as "addressed" and the incident as "not expected to be material". The Disclosure Letter admits there is no Bluefen consent, the debt is unpaid, and the incident scope is unknown. We should rely on the Disclosure Letter's admissions.

## Tier 1: Deal-critical issues

**1. Disclosure and buyer-knowledge provisions (Sch 7, cl 8.3, DL 1.1–1.2)**
- The Seller discloses the entire data room, the Accounts and public registers against all warranties. Clause 8.3 then bars any claim for matters the Buyer or its advisers knew of, or could have discovered from the data room or public records.
- Together these mean a warranty is only worth something for matters nobody could find. The warranties become close to illusory.
- Because the specific risks (Bluefen, Riverlark, Ironquay, incident) are all disclosed, warranty claims on them would be barred. Protection must come from conditions, price adjustments and specific indemnities.
- **Push back:**
  - Disclosure only if specific, fair and sufficiently detailed to identify the nature and scope of the matter.
  - No general disclosure of the data room or public registers.
  - Delete the constructive-knowledge language.
  - Add an express clause that the Buyer's rights are unaffected by its knowledge or investigation.
  - No knowledge defence at all for indemnities, title, capacity and tax.
- The disclosure date is 22 September 2026, over six weeks old. We need a frozen copy of the data room as the agreed disclosure set, and a bring-down at Completion. Between signing and Completion the Seller should have to notify new matters, and we should have a termination right for material ones.
- DL para 11 ("the Buyer must evaluate the disclosed facts") shifts the burden to us. Reject it.

**2. Limitations applied to everything (cl 9.3, 12.3, 12.8, 13, 20.5; Title)**
- The Seller wants one cap and time limit across all "Claims", the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance provisions to apply to "all Claims of any nature", and title and capacity under the same 20% / 18-month regime.
- That would limit title to AUD 4.8m and 18 months on a AUD 24m purchase of 100% of the shares. It would also catch indemnities, tax and fraud.
- **Push back:**
  - Limits apply only to general Warranty Claims.
  - Title and capacity are capped at 100% of the price and run for at least 6 years, which matches the NSW contractual limitation period (please verify).
  - Express carve-outs from all limits and from the exclusive-remedy and non-reliance clauses for fraud, wilful concealment, specific indemnities and the Seller's covenants.
  - Preserve rights to terminate before Completion, to seek specific performance and injunctions, and to bring statutory claims.
- Non-reliance clauses do not reliably exclude statutory misleading-conduct claims (Australian Consumer Law, Corporations Act s 1041H). We should not depend on that and should draft the carve-outs expressly.

**3. Bluefen (cl 3 / 6.3)**
- Bluefen is about AUD 3.6m of FY26 revenue, roughly 30%. Illustratively, the implied multiple of about 2x revenue puts around AUD 7m of value on that relationship.
- The Seller offers "reasonable endeavours" and deems the condition satisfied on delivery of any written consent. But DD-002 cl 11.3 attaches conditions, and the Disclosure Letter admits there is no final consent and no evidence the conditions are met.
- **Push back:**
  - Make the consent a condition precedent to Completion, in a form acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably.
  - It must be unconditional, or its conditions acceptable to us, with no adverse change to price, term or exclusivity.
  - Only the Buyer may waive the condition.
  - Add a long-stop date and a termination right.
  - The Seller bears the cost, and we take part in the communications.
  - If the Seller will not agree, seek a retention or contingent price reduction tied to Bluefen's position.

**4. Riverlark and the funds flow (cl 2 / 7)**
- The facility is about AUD 3.2m. The Seller proposes a release after Completion, which is inconsistent with a debt-free/cash-free deal.
- We would own a company with the debt and security still in place, and potentially a change-of-control default under DD-003 cl 8.1.
- **Push back:**
  - Repay at Completion from the proceeds under a payoff letter that includes interest, fees and break costs.
  - The discharge and release documents are signed and held in escrow before Completion, with PPSR (and any other registered security) discharges lodged on Completion.
  - Confirm the shares are not also charged.
  - Define "Net Debt" and deduct it from the price.
- The Seller's statement that the funds flow "reflects the agreed price mechanics" is not accurate. We have not agreed those mechanics, and the funds flow must be rebuilt.

**5. DD-006 data incident (cl 4.6 / Sch 6)**
- Roughly 1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) went to an unintended external address. It is unknown whether anyone accessed the file, what the scope is, or whether notification is required.
- "Not expected to be material" is the Seller's opinion, not a finding.
- With revenue of about AUD 12m, the Company is likely outside the Privacy Act small-business exemption. The Notifiable Data Breaches scheme probably applies, with a 30-day assessment period from when the Company became aware.
- If awareness was on or before about 7 October, that window has already passed. We need the awareness date.
- Customer contracts, Bluefen in particular, may also carry breach-notification duties.
- **Push back:**
  - A specific indemnity for all losses from the incident, outside the cap and thresholds and surviving at least 6 years. It should cover regulatory, notification, forensic and claim costs and customer loss.
  - The Seller completes the investigation and gives us the forensic report before Completion.
  - Any required notifications are made in a form we approve.
  - Consider a retention while the position is open.
  - Request the cyber-insurance policy and confirm whether the insurer has been notified.

**6. Ironquay IP (cl 11.1)**
- DD-004 cl 7.3 makes transfer of the SOW3 Project Materials conditional on cleared payment of every SOW3 fee. AUD 180,000 is recorded as open (DD-010), but there is no bank verification, no receipt and no confirmatory assignment.
- The existing indemnity covers only the payment. The real risk is that the Company does not own the IP, and a payment indemnity does not fix that.
- **Push back:**
  - Before Completion: evidence of cleared payment, and a signed deed of assignment from Ironquay (copyright assignments must be in writing and signed) with moral-rights consents.
  - A broader IP indemnity covering title defects, infringement claims and re-creation costs.
  - The Seller pays the AUD 180k or it is deducted from the price.
  - Diligence all other Ironquay SOWs for the same pattern.

## Tier 2: Material commercial points

**7. Completion bonuses (DD-005, AUD 420,000).** The Seller says this is "a matter for the Seller" but leaves it out of the funds flow. The Company is the obligor, so we would bear it. Treat it as a transaction cost or debt-like item and deduct it. Add employer on-costs: super (currently 12%) and NSW payroll tax could add roughly AUD 70–75k, subject to checking whether the bonuses attract them. The Disclosure Letter does not say.

**8. Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k aggregate).** Three renewals of AUD 110k each, which the Disclosure Letter says to read "together for timing/scope". The Seller calls them "ordinary course" but has not said whether they are committed, terminable or accrued.
- Obtain the contracts and test whether this is one commitment split into three.
- If committed or accrued and unpaid at Completion, treat them as debt-like or in working capital.
- Add an interim-period covenant that no contract above a set value may be entered into or renewed without our consent, with related contracts aggregated.

**9. Tax and IP "settled".** They are not. We want:
- A standalone pre-Completion tax indemnity (income tax, GST, PAYG, super, payroll tax, any R&D offset claims), capped at the price and surviving at least 6 years.
- IP warranties (ownership, contractor and employee assignments, open-source, non-infringement) at a higher cap and a longer period than the general warranties.

**10. Cap, thresholds and period**
- Cap of 20% (AUD 4.8m). The known quantifiable items alone (Riverlark, bonuses, Ironquay, Sandbar) total about AUD 4.13m, which shows how thin this is. Counter at 40–50% for general warranties, and expect to settle around 30–40%.
- Basket of AUD 250k, deductible. Counter with a tipping basket (first-dollar recovery) of about 0.5% of price (AUD 120k).
- De minimis of AUD 25k. Counter at AUD 10k, with related claims aggregated.
- 18-month period. Ask for 24 months so two audit cycles are covered.

**11. Recourse.** Harbourglass is a holding vehicle that can distribute the proceeds. We need a retention or escrow (for example 10% for 18–24 months), a parent or ultimate-owner guarantee, or W&I insurance. W&I will exclude the known matters, so the specific indemnities are still needed.

## Tier 3: Verify

- **Title (DD-012).** The Seller relies on its own share register. Require ASIC searches, share transfer forms, a constitution check for pre-emption or transfer restrictions, confirmation of no options, convertible notes or encumbrances, and a PPSR search over the shares.
- **Lease (DD-007) and Mossvale (DD-009).** The Seller says nothing requires consent, but the Disclosure Letter says only that the material does not describe a consent requirement. Check whether either document treats a change of control as an assignment. Require a specific warranty and, if needed, a consent condition. Calendar the lease notification.

## Recommended response

| # | Position to take |
|---|---|
| 1 | Reject "negotiated positions" framing; reserve all rights; request full SPA text |
| 2 | Specific, fair disclosure only; delete data-room and public-register general disclosure; delete cl 8.3 constructive knowledge; add pro-buyer knowledge clause; frozen data room set and bring-down |
| 3 | Limitations apply to general warranties only; title, capacity, tax, indemnities and fraud carved out; title at 100% of price, 6+ years |
| 4 | Bluefen consent is a Buyer-waivable condition precedent with long-stop and termination right |
| 5 | Riverlark repaid at Completion with escrowed discharge; Net Debt deducted from price; rebuild funds flow |
| 6 | Specific uncapped indemnity and forensic report for DD-006; confirm awareness date and notification status |
| 7 | Ironquay: payment evidence and signed assignment before Completion; broader IP indemnity |
| 8 | Bonuses (plus on-costs) and unpaid Ironquay fee treated as price deductions; Sandbar contracts diligenced and treated accordingly |
| 9 | Standalone tax indemnity; strengthened IP warranties |
| 10 | Counter on cap (30–50%), tipping basket (~AUD 120k), de minimis (AUD 10k), 24-month period |
| 11 | Retention, guarantee or W&I for recourse |
| 12 | Complete title, lease and Mossvale verification before signing |

Indicatively, the Riverlark debt, bonuses and Ironquay fee total about AUD 3.8m (plus on-costs). Together with any Sandbar adjustment, they bring the equity price well below the AUD 24m headline. The next step is to get the SPA text and the DD source documents so I can draft the mark-up and a price-adjustment schedule.
